findings.problem: The sign argument for the two partners is factored into permSignInt_swap_trans. The other two properties are proved twice. These are the involution property (swap, then swap again, cancels via trans_assoc, swap_swap, refl_trans) and fixed-point-freeness (evaluate the permutation at the left swap point and use swap_apply_left plus injectivity). Each pair has the same structure, differing only in the permutation type, Fin p versus Fin (p-1), and in the swap points. Any further partner, such as a top-label pairing, would repeat the pattern again.
findings.proposed_change: Add a generic lemma next to permSignInt_swap_trans, for example `theorem swap_trans_ne {n : Nat} (σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) (i j : Fin n) (hij : i ≠ j) : (Equiv.swap i j).trans σ ≠ σ`. Prove it by `intro h; have := congrArg (fun τ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n) => τ i) h; simp only [Equiv.trans_apply, Equiv.swap_apply_left] at this; exact hij (σ.injective this).symm`. Add a second lemma `swap_trans_swap_trans (σ) (i j) : (Equiv.swap i j).trans ((Equiv.swap i j).trans σ) = σ`. Prove it by `rw [← Equiv.trans_assoc, Equiv.swap_swap, Equiv.refl_trans]`. Then bottomPartner_ne becomes `fun h => swap_trans_ne z.bottom _ _ (firstCutLabels_ne hp z) (congrArg Code.bottom h)`. removalPartner_ne becomes `fun h => swap_trans_ne z.removal _ _ (eQ_castSucc_ne_succ hp i) (congrArg Code.removal h)`. The removalPartner_involutive removal goal closes with swap_trans_swap_trans. The bottom involution still needs the swap_comm step after the label rewrites, then the same lemma.
findings.benefit: The cancellation and fixed-point arguments are stated once, next to the existing sign lemma. The two pairings then differ only in their data, and the three properties (involution, no fixed points, sign reversal) are each discharged by one shared lemma. This makes the structure clear and shortens the proofs. The gain is modest because each duplicated block is short.
